For example, if I have a raidz of 4 disks (so 25% of space "wasted"), and add another disk, new data will be distributed on 5 disks (so 20% of space "wasted") but the old data will keep using stripes of 4 blocks, they will just be reshuffled between the disks. story: OpenZFS – Incremental add of disks to existing RAIDZ
text: That is not how this will work. The reason the parity ratio stays the same, is that all of the references to the data are by DVA (Data Virtual Address, effectively the LBA within the RAID-Z vdev). So the data will occupy the same amount of space and parity as it did before. All stripes in RAID-Z are dynamic, so if your stripe is 5 wide and your array is 6 wide, the 2nd stripe will start on the last disk and wrap around. So if your 5x10 TB disks are 90% full, after the expansion they will contain the same 5.4 TB of data and 3.6 TB of parity, and the pool will now be 10 TB bigger. New writes, will be 4+2 instead, but the old data won't change (they is how this feature is able to work without needing block-pointer rewrite). See this presentation: [VIDEO]
